deviations: Sizes against the TD-006 guide: token_ui.gd is 320 lines (78 doc, 205 code) against about 280 and token_ui_kit.gd 160 against about 150 (token_layout.gd 251 is inside). Five checks over four Rounds of real keys, a throwaway-controller check and the house rule of a doc on every declaration do not fit in less without dropping evidence; I cut what was redundant (a by-hand signal pass in T28, a reach loop, a duplicate premise). Three token_ui functions are over a rough cc of 10 (_idle_screens 15, _end_round 15, _restart 25) because their conditions are the assertions themselves, the TD-006 pattern; no function is over 40 lines.

T29 matrix: the delivery is by Player 2 ('Player 2 wins!') and the single loss is Player 1's ('Player 2 wins!'), as designed; I added Round four (Player 2 loses, 'Player 1 wins!') so a winner line that always names Player 2 is killed, and Round three is the real double loss ('Nobody wins!').

T27's Round-over panel with nobody_text is shown by emitting round_over(-1) by hand on the live controller (a real double loss at this stock needs 100 destructions each); the scenario says so in its header and detail, and token_ui T29 covers the real double loss. T27 also writes the Tokens label with every type's name and counts 0, 9, 10, 99, 100 as a capacity probe (the game only shows the carrier's name) and puts the label's own text back.

T28: PlayerHud._ready() runs before SplitScreen calls begin(), so the live HUD's pre-begin state cannot be observed afterwards; the check therefore builds a HUD, a PlayerChoiceInput and a UnitChoice from the scenes' own packed scenes on throwaway MatchController nodes (live rules, Units, Bases, cameras): one never begun, one begun with a null stock, one with a stock without a Motorbike Token. The live Units are untouched (the refusals bench nothing, and the rest of the run, which stands on live Units, passes). Its two ERROR lines on stderr are the refusals under test, so dev08.py new prints two ERR lines for token_ui; the CHECK and RESULT lines avoid the engine's capitalised words so a noise filter does not mistake them.

After a loss Player 1's cursor rests on the Buggy (the exhausted Motorbike made it snap, design 13.4) and stays there across R, so a bare fire key would choose the Buggy: after each R the scenario steers both cursors to the Motorbike with the real steer key before it presses the fire keys (the cursors found are printed in T30).
UiKit.bound_restart_key() reads round_restart's first event when it is a key (the screen reads its first key event); equal for the shipped Input Map.

Check names carry the design id in front (T25_hud_on_destruction_tick ...), as the tokens scenario does. T25 reads each Player's line inside the unit_destroyed handler (connected after every UI node), a frame later, and with the Unit still in play before the Self-destruct key (cursor on a Truck): the 5,4,3,2,1,0 sequence is the in-play 5 plus the five destruction readings 4..0; with two Players destroyed in one frame only the first handler's own line is judged there, because the second Player is not yet destroyed when it fires.
